title: Career Roadmap: Quantitative Analyst (Quant Analyst)
summary: A Quantitative Analyst applies mathematics, statistics, programming and financial theory to analyse financial markets, evaluate risk, develop trading strategies and support investment decisions.

facts.Current degree: BS (Research) – Physics / Chemistry / Mathematics / Biology / Materials Science

about.label: Primary Domains
about.text: Quantitative Finance, Financial Modelling, Trading, Risk Analytics, Investment Research

about.label: Suitable For
about.text: Students who enjoy mathematics, probability, statistics, analytical problem-solving and programming

blocks.text: A Quantitative Analyst applies mathematics, statistics, programming and financial theory to analyse financial markets, evaluate risk, develop trading strategies and support investment decisions.
Quants work with large datasets and mathematical models to identify patterns, estimate probabilities, value financial instruments and measure potential losses.
Typical responsibilities

items.text: Develop mathematical and statistical models for financial markets.
Analyse stock prices, derivatives, interest rates and other financial data.
Build and backtest quantitative trading strategies.
Measure market, credit and portfolio risks.
Use Python, SQL and statistical techniques to analyse datasets.
Evaluate model accuracy, assumptions and limitations.
Collaborate with traders, portfolio managers, data scientists and risk teams.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: A BS (Research) degree can provide a strong foundation, particularly in Mathematics, Physics or Statistics-related subjects. However, many quantitative analyst positions require advanced mathematical skills, programming experience and sometimes a master's or PhD. A bachelor's degree alone does not guarantee eligibility for every quant role.
Recommended undergraduate route
BS (Research) in Mathematics
Most direct route
Focus on calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, optimisation and numerical methods.
BS (Research) in Physics
Strong quantitative alternative
Build on mathematical modelling, differential equations, computation and numerical analysis.
BS (Research) in Chemistry, Biology or Materials Science
Possible with additional preparation
Strengthen mathematics, probability, statistics, algorithms and programming to meet quantitative-finance requirements.
Depending on the target role and admission eligibility, consider:

items.text: MSc Mathematics, Applied Mathematics or Statistics
MSc Quantitative Finance or Financial Mathematics
MSc Computational Science or Scientific Computing
MSc Data Science or a closely related quantitative discipline
MTech/MS in Computational Finance, Financial Engineering or a related field, where available and eligible
PhD in Mathematics, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Physics or a related quantitative field for research-intensive roles

blocks.text: Choose a postgraduate programme based on its mathematical depth, programming curriculum, research opportunities and placement outcomes—not just its title.
Year 1 — Mathematical Foundations

items.text: Strengthen calculus, linear algebra and introductory probability.
Learn Python fundamentals, functions, data structures and NumPy.
Study descriptive statistics and basic financial-market concepts.
Practise solving mathematical and logical problems.

blocks.label: Mini-project
blocks.text: Analyse historical stock prices and calculate returns, volatility and correlations.
Year 2 — Statistics and Programming

items.text: Study probability distributions, statistical inference and regression.
Learn pandas, SciPy, Matplotlib and SQL.
Understand hypothesis testing, time-series data and sampling bias.
Learn introductory algorithms and data structures.

blocks.label: Project
blocks.text: Compare the performance and risk of a group of stocks using historical data.
Year 3 — Quantitative Finance

items.text: Learn portfolio theory, risk measures and financial derivatives.
Study optimisation, numerical methods and time-series analysis.
Implement a strategy backtesting framework in Python.
Learn the basics of transaction costs, liquidity and market impact.

blocks.label: Project
blocks.text: Backtest a clearly defined trading strategy with realistic costs and an out-of-sample evaluation.
Year 4 — Research and Job Preparation

blocks.label: Select a focus
blocks.text: quantitative research, risk modelling, pricing or systematic trading.

items.text: Complete a research project using a documented dataset and reproducible code.
Apply for quantitative research, model-risk, financial analytics and relevant research internships.
Prepare for probability, statistics, coding and mathematical reasoning interviews.
Evaluate whether a specialised master's degree would improve access to target roles.

blocks.text: Adapt the sequence to the actual length and syllabus of the student's BS (Research) programme.

rows.text: Calculus, linear algebra, optimisation, differential equations
Random variables, distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing
Stochastic processes, numerical methods, Monte Carlo simulation
Python, NumPy, pandas, SciPy, object-oriented programming
SQL, data cleaning, validation and reproducible workflows
Equities, bonds, derivatives, portfolio theory and market structure
Regression, classification, time-series validation and model evaluation
Experimental design, documentation, model limitations and independent testing

blocks.label: Priority
blocks.text: Mathematics, probability, statistics and programming should come before advanced machine learning or complex trading models.
Quantitative Research Analyst
Develops and tests statistical hypotheses and mathematical models for market behaviour and investment strategies.

blocks.label: Best suited to
blocks.text: strong mathematics, statistics and research skills.
Quantitative Trading Analyst
Studies market signals, trading rules, execution costs and strategy performance.

blocks.label: Best suited to
blocks.text: probability, coding, rapid analytical reasoning and market knowledge.
Quantitative Risk Analyst
Builds models to estimate market, portfolio and other financial risks and assess stress scenarios.

blocks.label: Best suited to
blocks.text: statistics, modelling, careful validation and financial-risk concepts.
Derivatives Pricing Analyst
Uses mathematical models and numerical methods to value options and other financial instruments.

blocks.label: Best suited to
blocks.text: calculus, probability, stochastic processes and numerical computation.
Quantitative Developer
Implements quantitative models and financial research systems using efficient, reliable software.

blocks.label: Best suited to
blocks.text: programming, algorithms, numerical methods and software engineering.

Potential employers include investment banks, quantitative trading firms, hedge funds, asset managers, financial technology companies and risk-modeling teams. Entry requirements differ substantially between employers and job families.
Build a portfolio that demonstrates mathematical reasoning, clean code, testing and the ability to explain results.

rows.text: Linear algebra, optimisation and portfolio theory
Probability, numerical methods and financial mathematics
Time-series analysis, validation and transaction-cost modelling
Statistical learning and careful out-of-sample testing

blocks.text: Internship targets
Search for opportunities such as:

items.text: Quantitative research intern
Financial risk analytics intern
Model validation intern
Quantitative developer intern
Data science or statistical research intern
Financial markets research intern

blocks.text: For students without prior finance experience, a statistics, data science or scientific-computing internship can be a useful stepping stone.

blocks.label: Project quality matters
blocks.text: avoid presenting a profitable historical backtest as proof of future returns. Document data leakage risks, transaction costs, assumptions and out-of-sample results.
Certifications can supplement a strong academic and project portfolio, but they do not replace mathematical competence or practical experience.

blocks.label: CFA Program
blocks.text: useful for broader investment knowledge; it is not a substitute for quantitative research preparation.

blocks.label: FRM
blocks.text: relevant to financial risk management, subject to the programme's current requirements.

blocks.label: Python and scientific computing courses
blocks.text: prioritise practical use of NumPy, pandas, SciPy and statistical libraries.

items.text: Probability, statistics and optimisation courses: especially valuable for technical interviews.
Financial derivatives and quantitative finance courses: useful after building the mathematical foundation.

blocks.text: Before enrolling, check the provider's current syllabus, assessment format, fees and eligibility conditions.

Junior Quant Analyst / Quantitative Research Analyst / Risk Analyst

Quantitative Researcher / Senior Quant Analyst / Quantitative Developer

Progression depends on demonstrated ability, performance, role requirements and employer structure. Some research-intensive positions favour postgraduate qualifications.

items.text: Machine-learning-assisted quantitative research
Alternative-data analysis for investment research
Automated portfolio construction and risk monitoring
Derivatives pricing and computational finance
High-performance quantitative computing
Model validation, explainability and model-risk governance

blocks.text: AI tools can help with coding and exploratory analysis, but a quant must still verify mathematical assumptions, test data quality and understand why a model works—or fails.
Preparation progress
0 of 9 completed
Complete calculus, linear algebra and probability foundations
Build practical Python and SQL skills
Learn statistical inference and time-series analysis
Understand financial markets, portfolios and derivatives
Publish at least three well-documented quantitative projects
Complete a backtesting or risk-modelling project with realistic assumptions
Practise mathematics, statistics and coding interview problems
Apply for relevant internships or research opportunities
Assess postgraduate options against target employers' requirements
Final Recommendation

For a student pursuing a BS (Research) in Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology or Materials Science, the strongest route toward quantitative analysis is to build a rigorous foundation in mathematics, probability, statistics and Python, then apply these skills to financial modelling and research projects.

Students specialising in Mathematics or Physics may find the transition more direct, while students from other science disciplines should plan additional quantitative coursework. A relevant master's degree can be beneficial for highly mathematical research and trading positions, depending on the employer's requirements.
